newsitem.title: USA: World Bank denies Wolfensohn planning to leave job.
newsitem.headline: World Bank denies Wolfensohn planning to leave job.

text.p: The World Bank on Monday denied a magazine report that President James Wolfensohn was planning to leave the organization.
"We deny this completely," Bank spokesman Klas Bergman said.

Business Week magazine reported in its latest edition that Wolfensohn had "tired" of the World Bank post after 16 months on the job and was lobbying for a top position in the Clinton administration if the president is re-elected in November.
Bergman said Wolfensohn believes that he has a lot of work left to do at the World Bank.
Business Week also reported that top White House economist Joseph Stiglitz might be moving to the World Bank.
It said that Stiglitz, who chairs the White House's Council of Economic Advisers, was in line to become the World bank's chief economist.
Bergman said that no one has been offered that job yet.
Michael Bruno currently holds the post but is expected to step down soon.
